report.summary: The server gap was mostly a real memory leak, now fixed: each streamed request's render tree stayed subscribed to long-lived signals. RSS on admin now stays at about 500 MB over a soak. /admin/per-row, /admin/nested and /todos are well up on the first run, and DB round trips before first byte went from 4 to 2. The last 2 trips are the auth guard's session lookup, which decides the status code, so they remain and the "0 like Solid and Next" goal is not met. Also fixed: raw Postgres text reaching production pages, failed Boundaries stuck on their fallback, Boundaries running out of render passes, and modulepreload order. Starting the client during a stream was landed by another agent in 44fd6b4, built on my proposed protocol; I did not re-measure first working click. Open items: shape.browser streamed test timing out, Mac timings only, leak not re-run on yuna. All timing is from this Mac at load 13 to 26 and is directional only; first-run figures came from yuna-mbp, so before/after pairs cross machines. Patched-build numbers from the same Mac (per-row 49, /todos 80) are the fairer baselines where given.

fixes.problem: Server RSS reached 2.4 GB on admin and throughput collapsed on streamed pages (/admin/nested 20 req/s, /admin/per-row 16).
fixes.rootCause: A real leak, not eager loading. Boundary's content and fallback roots use createRoot(fn, parent), which doesn't register them on the parent, and on the server nothing disposed them. Their computations stayed subscribed to module-level signals such as a mutation's .pending. A heap snapshot traced markShipped.pending.node.o to retained Row objects, and heapUsed grew about 400 MB/s under load (about 2 MB per request). GC took 36% of CPU on /admin/orders.
fixes.change: Boundary now disposes its content and side roots in onCleanup. Later moved within async.ts by commit 44fd6b4; I checked it is still present. Tests: subscriber count after a streamed render, retained heap over repeated requests, a request cancelled mid-stream, and a client cleanup spy.

notFixed: Round trips before first byte are 2, not 0. They are Better Auth's two session queries, and a guard's redirect decides the status code. Solid gets 0 because its middleware only checks that a cookie exists and redirects later on the client.

Non-guard loads still run serially. A parent load can redirect, and nothing says which loads can't; the function-source heuristics I considered are fragile in a security check. In the templates this costs nothing: every page's load is synchronous after the session.

A query read outside any Boundary still holds the first byte (await s.settle() in page()). I did not build the early head. No template page has this shape, since their queries sit in Boundaries. Flushing early would also lose any header such a query sets.

Each landing still re-renders the whole page, because a Boundary's content can't render alone. /todos renders its shell at least twice. Fixing this is a change to the renderToStream design.

verdicts.fix: Postgres prepare per connection (c4a3811)
verdicts.why: Mechanism confirmed: the db test goes red with the default flipped to false and with the option ignored, but only when WEFT_TEST_POSTGRES is set, otherwise it skips. A column type change under a live statement still worked (retry). Gaps: (1) the statement cache is unbounded per connection: 300 inArray list lengths left 301 entries in pg_prepared_statements, and backend memory went from 2.0 MB to 10.4 MB against prepare:false. (2) Transactions are not covered: t.begin hands Drizzle the raw tx client, so 3 selects in a transaction added 0 prepared statements and still take describe plus bind. (3) Each pool connection describes once, and idle_timeout 20 s drops the statements (from reading, not timed). (4) Default true behind a transaction-mode pooler is unverified, pgbouncer is not installed here. I did not re-measure db.roundTrips 2.0.

fixes.problem: race.toggles failed on weft only: screen unchecked, database checked

fixes.change: Where calls overlap on an entry, their layers stay in order, replies don't land, and it reads once after the last answers. No extra read when nothing overlaps. Chose this over a server sequence because a stamp can't order commits across connections or instances, and it wouldn't fix the layer bug. A lost reply (not an FnError) also re-reads, since the write may have landed.

fixes.problem: Late reads reverted newer data, and in-flight first loads could not be invalidated (evidence item 1)
fixes.rootCause: From code and the reorder tests: setBase had no guard, load joined through `e.p ??=`, and staleTags matched on e.tags, which is empty during a first load.
fixes.change: A clock orders what reaches an entry. Reads and navigation entries older than it don't land, a rerun doesn't join an outdated read, and tags invalidated during a first load are checked against its answer. A read landing under a prediction waits, so a layer can't apply twice, and readers see the prediction while a read is out. seed takes `since`.
